A_open.text: Late August. Ravenwood, population: some people and a great many crows.
Ravenwood College. Dad's old stomping ground. And now, mine.
Gord: PUMPKIN SITUATION. CANT PICK UP. WALK. FOLLOW ROAD TO EDGE OF TOWN.
I don't own boots. I own three pairs of sneakers.
It's fine. It's a walk. How bad can a walk be?
Use the arrow keys to walk. Press Action to talk to people or look at things.

do.text: A notice: HOMECOMING IN OCTOBER! Beneath it: MISSING, one scarecrow. Reward: pumpkin.
Out of context, that's a lot of pumpkin.
The fountain is full of coins. And one pumpkin seed.
Why is there a pumpkin seed in the fountain? Wishes for a big harvest?

B_town.text: A crow lands on a lamppost and watches Brad with unnerving interest.
Hi there. Are you the welcome committee?
I'll take that as a yes.
Sunset is coming. Brad has time for two stops before it gets dark.

on_max.text: The sun slides behind the rooftops. Time to go.

else.text: I should really ask someone which way the farm is first.

stop_g.text: Welcome to the Grove Cafe! Oh, a new face! I know all the faces, so you're new!
Hi! Brad Bart. Could you point me to the McVine farm?
Gord's place? He grows my pumpkins! I'm Georgia Grove. Grove Cafe. We're not creative, we're consistent.
Oh, that's Biscuit at the window! He loves the day-olds.

then.text: The girl at the tavern called him Edgar.
He's got a lot of names. He's very popular.

stop_g.text: Here, take a cookie! Pumpkin spice. It's the house special.

stop_g.prompt: Georgia holds out a warm cookie.

do.text: It's warm. Warmer than a cookie should be. It tingles.
This is amazing. Is it supposed to tingle?
Tingly's a feature!
I miss my mom's meatloaf. And I don't even like meatloaf.
...Why did I say that?
Huh. Interesting.
What's interesting?
Nothing! Cookie! Enjoy!
I'm saving my appetite. I've heard Gord cooks a lot.
Smart! Here, for later.
She wraps the cookie in a napkin and tucks it into his bag anyway.

stop_g.text: Farm road is past the big oak. Look for the pumpkins.

stop_s.text: On the porch of the Log and Stump, a girl in black sweeps a floor that is already clean.
Hi! Sorry to bother you. Could you point me toward the McVine farm?
I... it's four in the afternoon.
The farm's up the road. Past where the streetlights give up.
How will I know I'm there?
The pumpkins will be judging you.
The crow lands on the Log and Stump sign. Sandra doesn't look up.
That's Edgar. He's not mine. He just likes the leftovers.

then.text: The cafe girl called him Biscuit.
He answers to anything with crumbs.

options.text: Earnest: Thanks! I'm so excited to be here!

do.text: Thanks! I'm Brad. I'm so excited to be here!
That's a lot of enthusiasm for four p.m.
Sandra. Stump. Like the sign. I don't know why we're a log and a stump either.

options.text: Joke: Closed to optimism? Open to sarcasm?

do.text: Closed to optimism? Tough. Are you open to sarcasm?
...We have a special on that.
Sandra Stump. Like the sign. Don't ask about the log.
Right. Thanks. Bye!
Smart.
Brad hurries off. He never got her name.

stop_p.text: At the college gate, a woman in glasses is glaring at a card reader.
I tapped it. I tapped it correctly. I have tapped it for eleven years.
It must have been replaced. Without notice. By ravens. Are you lost? You look lost.
Brad notices her badge is upside down.

do.text: Maybe try flipping it? The stripe is on the wrong side.
I knew that. I was testing the system.
Of course you were.
Should I call campus security?
No! Please! Last time they wrote a report.
In her panic she flips the badge. The gate beeps happily.
...It was upside down. You didn't see that.

stop_p.text: Thank you. Patricia Peters, Biology. And you are...?
Her smile freezes for exactly one second.
Welcome to Ravenwood, Mr. Bart. I'll see you at orientation.
And you. Don't look at me like that.

C_farm_road.text: The streetlights give up exactly where Sandra said they would.
It's getting dark. And the road is getting squishy.
Far ahead, something glows faintly orange.

do.text: McVINE PUMPKIN FARM. Est. 1954. Please do not pet the pumpkins.
Okay. No petting. Got it.

D_farm.text: The farm is enormous. Barn. Farmhouse. Pumpkins stacked like orange cannonballs.
That's a lot of pumpkins.
A redhead in a green tee leans on the fence, holding a clipboard and a grin.
It's a pumpkin farm. We're very committed to the concept.
You must be Brad! I'm Jane McVine, Gord's daughter. Welcome to the farm.
Nice shoes.
They're sneakers.
They're a cry for help. Wait here.
Jane returns from the porch with a pair of old work boots.
Dad kept these. They're your father's. Left behind sophomore year. He says they've been waiting.
Brad pulls them on. They fit. Almost suspiciously well.
Farm magic. Or large feet. Come on, first chore.
A wheelbarrow holds the biggest pumpkin Brad has ever seen. It's roughly the size of a small car.
That's Doris. Dad wants her in the barn before dark. Doris has a reputation.

do.text: On second thought, I'd love some help.
Good answer. Keep it low and push with your legs. Like carrying a very heavy opinion.
Together they roll Doris into the barn without incident. Doris seems disappointed.
I think she's judging me.
She's judging both of us.
I've got this.
Brad pushes. Doris wobbles. Brad pushes harder. Doris stops caring.
Doris tips into a haystack. Brad tips in after her.
That's the best entrance anyone's made all year!
I meant to do that.
Sure you did, city boy. Doris is fine. You're fine. The hay is surprised.

D_farm.text: A tall, bearded man steps out of the barn, wiping his hands on his jeans.
You're late.
Joking. Probably.

then.text: Fell in the hay, did you?

else.text: Good. Farming's a team sport. Mostly a team of pumpkins.

D_farm.text: I'm Gord. Uncle Gord, if you want. Gord, if you don't.
Uncle Gord. Thanks for letting me stay.
Your father says hello. In a letter. Eleven pages. I read the first.
He means he used the rest as a coaster.
...Also true.
That crow's been following me since the bus.
That's the Inspector. He inspects.

E_dinner.text: Dinner is soup. Also bread. Also pie. All pumpkin. Even the napkins are orange.
Don't ask questions you can't unsee.
Pumpkins have been acting strange this year.
He says it the way other people say the weather is nice.

E_dinner.prompt: Gord says something odd with a straight face.

do.text: Strange how? Like... big strange?
Growing fast. Too fast. Some nights they hum.
Dad.
...Eat your soup.
Hum?
Pumpkins hum. It's a farm thing. Don't think about it.
Ha! Good one.
...Yes. A joke.
Dad jokes are rare. Treasure it.
I'll treasure it.

E_dinner.text: Night, Brad. Welcome to the farm.

F_attic.text: The attic room is small and warm. It smells like hay and old books.
Dad slept here once. Probably in these boots.
Day one. Pumpkins are judgmental. Boots matter. And something strange is going on in this town.
The crow lands on the windowsill.
Far across the dark fields, something glows faintly orange.
It pulses once. Twice. Then it fades.
